description:
## Goal

Two valid `Enum.reduce/3` calls must keep each reducer closure correlated with the enumerable element family that supplied its arguments, even when both calls start from the underconstrained `[]` accumulator.

## Current state

At origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, this valid program is rejected by interp, JIT, and AOT compilation:

```fz
fn main() do
  dbg(Enum.reduce([1, 2], [], fn (x, acc) -> [x + 10 | acc] end))
  dbg(Enum.reduce(["a", "b"], [], fn (x, acc) -> [x <> "!" | acc] end))
end
```

Elixir 1.19.4 accepts and executes the equivalent program. Each reduce call also succeeds when compiled alone.

Together, FZ reports at the integer reducer:

```text
error[spec/violation]: call to `+/2` violates its @spec for arguments (binary, int)
```

Swapping source order does not remove the failure.

`Enum.reduce/3` wraps the supplied reducer at `runtime:Enum.fz:14-16`. Public telemetry names the two user lambdas separately, but later derives crossed wrapper activations such as:

```text
closure[binary reducer](), int, list(int)
closure[integer reducer](), binary, empty_list()
```

That second crossed activation invokes the integer reducer with `(binary, empty_list())`, manufacturing the false `+/2` violation. The problem is correlation loss in activation/call evidence, not a wrong `+/2` contract and not an invalid reducer.

## Strategy

Trace the crossed activation backward from the `Enum.reduce/3` wrapper through closure-call resolution and activation-input joining. Preserve the relationship between the captured reducer identity and the element/accumulator row instead of suppressing diagnostics in user reducer bodies. Do not special-case `+/2`, binary concatenation, or `Enum.reduce/3` syntax.

## Signal / acceptance

1. Add a red-first three-door behavioral fixture for the reproducer, with an Elixir oracle. `interp`, `run`, and the built executable all exit 0 and produce the two correct reduced lists.
2. Add a semantic/telemetry regression proving neither user lambda receives an activation containing the sibling call's element family.
3. Keep the integer-only and binary-only controls green.
4. Keep genuine invalid arithmetic diagnostics green; the fix must remove the manufactured argument row, not weaken `spec/violation`.
5. Re-run the dispatch stress relevant to the original bycatch: `arms:reverse`, `arms:1`, `arms:6`, `wrappers:1`, `wrappers:6`, `1`, and `6`. The fixed fixture must retain identical success/output.
6. Update the applicable semantic/type-specialization documentation and run formatting, clippy with warnings denied, focused tests, full library/CLI tests, and the fixture matrix.

comments.text: CONCORDANCE (2026-09-03): this ticket's reproducer IS the defect fz-kdt.183 now names precisely -- List.reduce_step/3 keyed on free type variables shares one activation and one joined return across every Enum.reduce/3 user (its list slot is forwarded to reduce_cont/3, whose key is ground in the element, so the element decides the return and the key erased it); the phantom `+/2 (binary, int)` is the joined row reaching the user lambda. The fz-kdt.124 review's attacks a1/b1 are this program's shape; the HEAD FATAL variant (two same-driver reducers, panic at artifact.rs:154) is recorded on 183. Owned by fz-kdt.183: this program is one of its red-first gates (three doors, both source orders). Closes when 183 lands.

title: Enum.reduce/3 cross-pairs reducer identity and element type across calls sharing an [] accumulator
